column1: # Pre-orchestrator delivery surface: workflows that perform a state-mutating
# invocation without being generated from a delivery() declaration (#1794 is
# what happens when one of these drifts out of the gate everything around it
# Consumed by tools/conformance/check.sh (check_delivery, arm c -- the
# side-effect firewall): every workflow under .github/workflows/ matching
#   pulumi up | bazel run ...:(deploy|up|apply) | helm push | gh release upload
# must be EITHER the generated .github/workflows/delivery.yaml OR listed here
# with a justification. A NEW unlisted match fails the check; a row whose
# workflow no longer matches also fails (stale exception), the same policy
# public-targets.tsv and version-pins.tsv apply -- so this file can only ever
# shrink, and the delivery surface can never silently grow.
# TWO CLASSES OF ROW, after Phase 2:
#   "dispatch-only shell — ..."  the push (and release) lanes are MIGRATED; the
#       file survives one release cycle as the break-glass escape hatch and is
#       DELETED in Phase 3, taking its row with it.
#   "PERMANENT — ..."            the hard floor Phase 3 stops at: reusable
#       workhorses the generated workflow calls, the foundation ladder (spec §3
#       non-goal), repo governance, dispatch-only manual ops, and release
#       machinery. These rows are the answer to "why is this not orchestrated",
#       and the conformance check keeps them honest either way: a row whose
#       workflow no longer mutates is itself a failure.
